items.stem: An unbiased estimate of the population variance from a sample of size n is
Explain why dividing by n − 1 rather than n gives an unbiased estimate of the population variance.
items.answer: Deviations are measured from the sample mean, which is closer to the data than the population mean, so Σ(x − x̄)² tends to underestimate Σ(x − μ)²; dividing by n − 1 corrects this so the expected value equals σ².
items.markingKey: B1 deviations from x̄ are too small on average; B1 n − 1 makes E(s²) = σ² [2]

items.stem: Explain what is meant by an unbiased estimate of a population parameter.
items.answer: An estimate from a statistic whose expected value (mean over all possible samples) equals the parameter.
items.markingKey: B1 expected value; B1 equals parameter [2]
